- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or adjust downward by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses late-period momentum; weight recent 7–10 days more heavily in smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.5) and prices are rising, model may lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if no clear reversal.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days are flat or declining, reduce forecast slope to prevent false upticks.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% noise in forecast to capture short-term swings.
